reports.title: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with our interim condensed consolidated financial statements (unaudited) and the notes thereto included elsewhere in this report.

lines: The facility is expected to be drawn upon delivery of each vessel in separate tranches of $22.0 million each with drawdowns expected between the fourth quarter of 2027 and the first quarter of 2029.

In addition, $1.9 million of amortization related to prior service cost and net loss is expected to be reclassified to “Other (expenses)/income, net” during the twelve-month period ending September 30, 2027.

desk.headline: Revenue up 9% to $284.3m and adjusted EPS up 23% to $8.32, above estimates; backlog a record $5.0bn, no financial guidance
results: Revenue rose $23.6m to $284.3m, above the $274.0m estimate; containership revenue grew 4% to $247.8m, helped by new deliveries and less off-hire.
Drybulk revenue jumped 69% to $36.5m as daily earnings per vessel rose to $32,690 from $19,910 on a stronger Capesize market.
Adjusted EPS was $8.32 (vs $6.75); GAAP EPS of $9.64 also includes gains on its Star Bulk and Yoda shareholdings.
Danaos took delivery of three new containerships, ordered two more and now has 28 container and four drybulk ships on order.
In October it paid a $1.00 quarterly dividend plus a $5.00 special dividend; debt rose to $1.38bn as newbuild financing was drawn.

guidance.summary: Danaos gives no revenue or earnings guidance. Its container fleet is fully chartered for 2026 and 94% for 2027, which gives good visibility on revenue.

points: CEO John Coustas said scarce open tonnage keeps strengthening the charter market, with few ship deliveries in 2027 and a bigger wave in 2028.
Charters worth about $611m were added, taking backlog to a record $5.0bn with an average 4.5 years left on contracts.
Management expects Red Sea container traffic could resume in Q1 2027, seen mainly as a scheduling change rather than relief for congestion.
The planned Norwegian listing of a minority stake in the drybulk business was postponed to wait for a better market window.
The company remains committed to buybacks (about $65m left) but gave no timeline; net debt was $327.9m with about $1.24bn of liquidity.
